[Amended (2017-10-28, ka-model-bbl-2017:CHAPTER 2(2)(3)): 1.4 Mutatis mutandis application of Master Plan and Zonal Regulations: Pursuant to Clause 1(3) of Notification No. UDD 14 TTP 2017 (P-4) dated 28-10-2017 (published on the official GBA/BBMP Building Plan Approval System under Bye laws and Zoning Regulations), all mandatory Master Plan or Zonal Regulations regarding use, land use, coverage, FAR, setback or open space, height, number of stories, number of dwelling units, and parking standards for various categories of buildings, including all amendments or modifications made therein from time to time, apply mutatis mutandis as part of these Bye-laws.]

records.title: SAFETY MEASURES AGAINST EARTH QUAKE IN BUILDING CONSTRUCTION
records.text: SAFETY MEASURES AGAINST EARTH QUAKE IN BUILDING CONSTRUCTION Buildings with ground plus four floors and above or buildings with a height of 15 mtrs. and above shall be designed and constructed adopting the norms prescribed in the National Building Code and in the 'Criteria for earthquake resistant design of structures' bearing No. IS 1893-2002 published by the Bureau of Indian Standards, making the buildings resistant to earthquake. The supervision certificate and the completion certificate of every such building shall contain a certificate recorded by the Registered Engineer / Architect that the norms of the National Building Code and I.S. 1893-2002 have been followed in the design and construction of buildings for making the buildings resistant to earthquake. [Modified (2007-06-25, rmp2015-zr:9.3): 30.0 SAFETY MEASURES AGAINST EARTHQUAKE IN BUILDING CONSTRUCTION: Buildings with ground plus three floors and above or height of 11.5 m / 15.0 m and above shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the Indian Standard codes for earthquake-resistant design (IS 1893, IS 13920, IS 4326) and certified by a Registered Structural Engineer under Clause 30.0 and Chapter 9, Clause 9.3 of the RMP 2015 Zoning Regulations.]

records.title: Wherever any construction is in violation/deviation of the sanctioned plan, the Commissioner may, if he considers that the violations / deviations are within 5% of (1) the set back to be provided around the building, (2) plot coverage (3) floor area ratio and (4) height of the building and that the demolition under chapter XV of the Act is not feasible without affecting structural stability, he may regularise such violations/deviations after recording detailed reasons for the same.
records.text: (i) Wherever any construction is in violation/deviation of the sanctioned plan, the Commissioner (Bengaluru East City Corporation, Notification No: BECC/Com/PR/331/2026-27 dated 14-05-2026) may, if he considers that the violations / deviations are within the limits specified in Table-2B below (up to 15% setback and coverage deviation; up to 15% FAR deviation on plots up to 500 sq.m and 5% FAR deviation on plots above 500 sq.m; 7.5% height deviation not beyond sanctioned number of floors) in case of (1) the setback to be provided around the building, (2) plot coverage (3) floor area ratio and (4) height of the building and that the demolition under chapter XVII of the Act is not feasible without affecting structural stability, he may regularize such violations/deviations after recording detailed reasons for the same and levying compounding fee as per Table-2A, Table-2C and Table-2D (minimum guidance value consideration Rs.50,000/- per sq.m; Residential 3%/6% up to 500 sq.m and 5%/10% above 500 sq.m; Non-Residential 6%/12%).

records.title: Limitations of floor area and covered area
records.text: Under Revised Master Plan 2015 Volume III Zoning Regulations (effective 25-06-2007), the Local Planning Area of Bengaluru is organized into three main Rings (Ring I: Core Area within Core Ring Road; Ring II: Developed Area between Core Ring Road and Outer Ring Road; Ring III: Developing Area beyond Outer Ring Road) and zone-specific land-use categories in Chapter 4 (Tables 10–19), which govern maximum plot coverage and Floor Area Ratio (FAR) with reference to plot size and existing road width, superseding the 1995 CDP A, B and C areas and Table 6 of the 2003 Bye-laws.

records.text: Exterior open spaces / setbacks, coverage, floor area ratio, numbers of floors and heights: Under Section 76M of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 and Revised Master Plan 2015 Volume III Zoning Regulations (G.O. No. UDD 540 BEM AA SE 2004, effective 25-06-2007), the setbacks required on all sides of buildings up to 11.5 m height (plots up to 4000 sq.m) and high-rise buildings above 11.5 m height are governed by Chapter 3, Regulation 3.1 (Table 8: Exterior open spaces / setbacks in percentage of width/depth of plot, and Table 9: All-around setbacks for buildings above 11.5 m height) of the RMP 2015 Zoning Regulations, superseding Tables 4 and 5 of the 2003 Bye-laws.

records.title: High-rise buildings (11.5 m height and above)
records.text: In the case of high-rise buildings (11.5 m height and above), the minimum all-around front, rear, and side setbacks shall be as specified in Chapter 3, Regulation 3.1, Table 9 of the Revised Master Plan 2015 Zoning Regulations (effective 25-06-2007), starting at 5.0 m all-around for buildings above 11.5 m up to 15.0 m height and increasing progressively up to 16.0 m for buildings above 50.0 m height.
